title: C# Questions & Answers - Implementation of Exception Handling
sourceFile: Exception Handling Implementation - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on implementation of the exception handling in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: 1) i = -1: sum = 10 / -1 = -10. 2) i = 0: sum = -10 / 0 triggers a DivideByZeroException (ArithmeticException). 3) The catch block prints '0 '. 4) Finally, the current value of sum (-10) is printed. Output: '0 -10'.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The loop first prints all elements '12345'. Then, division by zero occurs, which is caught by ArithmeticException, printing 'B'. Result: '12345B'.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The loop prints '12345'. When i = 5, a[5] is accessed which is out of bounds, throwing IndexOutOfRangeException. The catch block prints '0'. Result: '123450'.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation: Division by zero occurs, throwing a DivideByZeroException. Since this inherits from ArithmeticException, it is caught and 'B' is printed.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: 1) i = -1: sum = -10, prints '-1 '. 2) i = 0: Division by zero occurs, jumping to catch block. 3) Catch prints '0'. Final output: '-1 0'.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation: The exception is caught by the catch block (printing 'B '), and the finally block is guaranteed to run afterward (printing 'C'). Result: 'B C'.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation: The index 10 is outside the range of the array (size 5). This throws an exception, which is caught, printing the first message. Then the code continues to the final line.

questions.question: If an exception is thrown at runtime and there is no matching 'catch' block in the code, who handles the exception?
questions.explanation: If no suitable catch block is found in the call stack, the CLR's default exception handler catches it, which usually results in displaying an error message and terminating the application.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The exception is caught. Inside catch, z = (2 * 5) - 10 = 0. The output is 'B 0'.

questions.question: Choose the correct statement about how exception handling works in C#.NET:

options.text: The runtime searches for a local catch handler where the exception occurred
If no local match is found, it walks up the call stack to find a handler
If no handler is found at any level, the program terminates with an unhandled exception

questions.explanation: This process is known as 'stack walking'. The .NET runtime systematically searches for a compatible catch block from the point of failure up through the sequence of method calls.
